page.layout: One page of running text in one column on the left. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the lines they stand by. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: &tis. Tum comparatis & exemplis aliorū. Sed quia hominis parū prudentis,aut moSententiæ de-nunciatio-num [illegible, ~6 letters] defti esse videtur,de futuris velle scribere, [illegible, ~10 letters] vt ille ait,funt Dei:opera quoq; danda est,ne temerè ac stultè, sed moratemorate & cōciliantes. atq; decoré agere videamur. Fit autè hoc quatuor potissimum modis.primo genere orationis:si scilicet non [illegible, ~6 letters] simpliciter & affeuerando,sed aut [illegible, ~8 letters] condi-tione,aut [illegible, ~7 letters] dubitatione quadam de futuris scribamus.Secundo [illegible, ~8 letters] mitigatione vel ante vel post adhibita,eadem que ostendamus, non nos affirmare hic quicquam,sed coniecturis solum quibus-dam niti.Tertiò [illegible, ~12 letters] caufæ re-motione: cum affirmamus, non temere hic nos aliquid asserere, sed nostras coniecturas scribere, vel ab amico rogatos, vel etiam quod existimemus eundem do lore impeditum de illis cogitare minimè posse.Postremò [illegible, ~7 letters] voto & precatione: si adiiciamus: futura in Dei Opt. Max. sita est manu: eundem nos rogare: vt vates vanos atq; falsos nos esse velit. Verum ne-Sententiæ [illegible, ~6 letters] mouentes. que motus hic erunt negligendi, sed duo potissimum excitandi: metus,& spes seu confidentia. Non enim propterea futura denunciantur,vt de iis certior solum ami

page.notes: Greek words in the running text and in the side notes could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible. The catchword and the running head are as printed; the head is given with u for the printed v. The "&tis" at the top of the page is a fragment continued from the previous page and was kept as printed. The last line "ami" is a fragment running on to the next page.
